memory_candidates.content: A surgical, line-oriented array-insertion technique for repairing a hand-maintained JSON array derived from a directory tree (e.g. manifest.json provides.scripts vs. an extension's tracked scripts/ dir), without a whole-document jq round-trip that would reformat unrelated content. Insert each missing entry at its LOCALLY alphabetical position relative to the EXISTING array's own order (first existing entry that sorts after it; append at the end if none), never resorting the pre-existing entries -- real hand-maintained arrays in a codebase are often only loosely/locally sorted (e.g. interleaving a script with its own test), so a full resort produces an unreviewable diff while local insertion keeps every --write a minimal, single-purpose change. The one case needing care: appending past the array's previous last entry requires adding a trailing comma to that one line (the only existing line whose text changes). This generalizes generate-context-line-counts.sh's own line-oriented repair pattern from a single-value substitution to a variable-length insertion.

When adding a narrowing filter to an existing branch of a two-sided gate (a filter that only shrinks a candidate set, never grows it), the correct fail-safe DIRECTION depends on which branch's existing default behavior the filter is narrowing -- it is not a universal constant. A filter narrowing an already-BLOCKING branch (e.g. 'is this candidate-new finding unrelated to the batch') must fail-safe toward STILL BLOCKING on ambiguous input (an identifier-free line is never cleared). A filter narrowing an already-PROCEEDING branch (e.g. 'is this pre-existing finding self-caused by the completing task') must fail-safe toward STILL PROCEEDING on the identical ambiguous input (an identifier-free line is never reported as self-caused), or it would brick every completion whenever any identifier-free red finding exists anywhere -- exactly the batch-wide brick the proceeding branch was designed to avoid in the first place. Both filters can share the identical identifier-scanning/matching logic (extract into one shared internal helper parameterized by a mode flag) while their external fail-safe behavior is deliberately mirror-image, not symmetric to each other in the way a naive reviewer might expect.
